title: Entitlement map: bounded domains and delegable actions
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: RBAC v1 has grown organically: coarse roles, implicit inheritance, and ad-hoc admin overrides. This ticket proposes an 'entitlement map' model designed to make authorization deterministic, auditable, and delegable across Redwood's hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Goals:
- Define a compact data model for entitlements: bounded resource domains, canonical action-sets, explicit bindings (principal -> domain -> actions), and short-lived elevations (breakglass).
- Make evaluation order explicit: direct bindings > delegated bindings > domain defaults; explicit deny always wins.
- Ensure the model is migration-friendly (v1 -> v2), supports SSO/SAML group transforms, and emits rich audit records for every decision.
- Provide clear API semantics for sync permission checks and async audit hooks used by Console and Dedicated control plane.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus on read/write/action-level permissions (e.g., model:deploy, runtime:stream, tenant:billing.view). Not covering attribute-based policies in this ticket, but the model should be extensible to attach attribute constraints later.
- Must work in multi-tenant mode: resource domains can be tenant-scoped or global.
- Performance budget: permission check P95 <= 2ms in typical runtime path with in-memory cache; fallback to DB for misses.

Design summary (high level):
1) Resource domains: namespaced containers representing a logical boundary (e.g., tenant:acme, org:infra, global:catalog). Domains have metadata: tenancy (tenant/global), parent (optional), and default action-set.
2) Action-sets: canonical list of actions grouped by surface (runtime, model-catalog, billing, admin). Each action has an id, implied scope (read/write/admin), and volatility flag (whether it may be elevated temporarily).
3) Bindings: tuple of (principal, domain, action-set, grant_type, metadata). grant_type = {direct, delegated, inherited}. Metadata includes source (SSO group, service-account, API-key), created_by, created_at, expires_at, justification.
4) Deny rules: explicit denies are first-class bindings with deny semantics and audit metadata.
5) Delegation: principals with delegation right can create delegated bindings but cannot grant actions marked non-delegable. Delegations are scoped with expiry and a chain-of-trust field for auditability.
6) Elevations (breakglass): ephemeral grants created via admin flow; must be logged with approver, TTL, and optional JIT justification. Elevations are evaluated with highest precedence for the TTL but flagged for post-hoc review.
7) Evaluation order: 1) explicit deny at principal level, 2) explicit allow at principal level, 3) delegations to principal, 4) domain defaults, 5) global defaults. Each step emits an audit decision event.
8) SSO/SAML mapping: transform pipeline maps incoming SAML attributes/groups to zero or more bindings. Transform rules are declarative (regex/group mapping) and applied at sync-time during SSO login and periodically by a reconcile job.
9) Audit schema: every permission check emits a single compact record with fields: timestamp, trace_id, actor, principal_id, resource_domain, action_id, decision (allow/deny), reason (binding id + type), pre_state (effective grants before request), post_state (if mutated), evaluation_path, service, and optional justification. Records are JSONL and pushed to internal audit stream and optional customer audit logs for Private deployments.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Simplicity vs expressiveness: chose compact domain + action-set model to avoid migration complexity and steady-state evaluation cost. Attribute-based rules are deferred.
- Performance vs full audit fidelity: auditing every micro-decision is costly; plan emits one decision event per check with compact references to binding ids instead of full binding payloads to keep size manageable.

Migration plan (high level):
- Import v1 roles into domain-scoped bindings using best-effort mapping; flag ambiguous mappings for manual review in Console.
- Run an offline simulation mode (30 days) to collect diffs between v1 and entitlement map decisions; surface in migration dashboard.
- Provide CLI tool and one-click Console helper to convert role-attachments to direct bindings with user verification.

Operational runbooks:
- Audit retention and export: default 90 days in hosted; customers can opt into longer retention for Dedicated/Private.
- Emergency revocation: support immediate global deny propagation with TTL-based rollbacks and guaranteed durability.

Open questions (tracked below):
- Should deny rules be allowed on parent domains to implicitly block an action for all children? (Pros: single place for org-wide restrictions; Cons: surprising override semantics)
- How to express temporal constraints beyond TTL (e.g., business-hours-only access)? Defer to future ABE ticket.

Deliverables for this ticket: design doc in Confluence, canonical JSON schema for entitlement records, a permission-check API spec, proof-of-concept in runtime with in-memory cache and hooks for audit emission, and a migration simulation job.
acceptance_criteria: Define entitlement map JSON schema covering domains, action-sets, bindings, denies, delegations, and elevations
Evaluation precedence documented and implemented in a reference permission-check module
Audit record schema finalized and emitted by POC for all evaluated checks (single JSONL per event)
SSO/SAML transform rules pipeline documented with examples and a reconcile job prototype
Migration simulation runs on existing tenant data and produces a reviewable diff report
End-to-end tests for delegation, explicit deny, and breakglass covering common edge cases
